title: Doors — Cargo Door Latch Shafts — Installation of Self-Lubricating Bushes

issue.reason: Initial issue of the self-lubricating latch bush bulletin.

abstract: Replacement of the greased latch shaft bushes by self-lubricating items on delivered aircraft, deleting the six-hundred-hour lubrication task and removing the door stiffness reports from wet-climate stations.

sections.planning_reason: Ground handling staff at wet-climate stations report increasing effort to close the cargo door, and a small number of doors have needed a second attempt to reach the latched position. In every investigated case the shaft bearing grease was washed out or diluted with de-icing fluid. The lubrication task that keeps the greased bush serviceable is due every six hundred flight hours and line stations are completing it late. Operators asked for a bearing that does not need lubrication rather than a stricter task.
sections.description: The greased bronze bushes in the four latch shaft bearings of each cargo door are replaced by self-lubricating liner bushes. The latch stiffener is machined to the new bore, the retaining angle is replaced by an item with a deeper spigot so that the bush is captive without staking, and the door warning sensor target plate is re-shimmed for the reduced shaft end float.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the cargo door in the maintenance position and make the door safe against inadvertent operation. Remove the latch access panels from inside the compartment in zones 831 and 891. Remove the four latch shafts and the retaining angle D5230139019163. Machine the bore of the latch stiffener D5230135108629 to the dimension given in the accomplishment instructions using the line reamer from the tooling set. Install the self-lubricating bushes and the new retaining angle, secured with blind rivets EN989730K5 and swaged collars LN181939-7B. Install the latch shafts and measure the end float. Shim the warning sensor target plate to the measured float. Do the cargo door operational test and the door warning system test. Remove the six-hundred-hour lubrication task for the latch shaft bearings from the aircraft maintenance schedule and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to aircraft MSN C00001 through C00319 that are pre modification standard. Aircraft delivered from MSN C00321 onward were built with the self-lubricating bushes and are not affected. One withdrawn aircraft is excluded.
sections.material_note: Kit K5230-1015-01 contains four bushes, the retaining angle, the rivet and collar set and the shim pack, and is supplied per door. Bushes must be replaced as a matched set of four; single-bush replacement is not permitted.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled A-check, or within 36 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

title: Doors — Cargo Door Latch Shafts — Installation of Self-Lubricating Bushes

issue.reason: Planning information extended with a concurrency recommendation for aircraft also eligible for the door surround corner reinforcement; instructions unchanged.
